modules.title: SQL JOINs, GROUP BY & HAVING
modules.subtitle: Aggregate relational data cleanly in a real live SQLite engine.
modules.summary: Master SQL execution order (`FROM -> WHERE -> GROUP BY -> HAVING -> SELECT -> ORDER BY`) and run real `.sql` queries from Neovim.

sections.title: 1.1 WHERE vs HAVING
sections.body: `WHERE` filters raw rows *before* grouping. `HAVING` filters aggregated groups *after* `GROUP BY` (for example, `HAVING AVG(score) >= 0.85`).
sections.code_example:
SELECT m.name, ROUND(AVG(r.score), 2) AS avg_score
FROM models m
JOIN eval_runs r ON r.model_id = m.id
GROUP BY m.name
HAVING AVG(r.score) >= 0.85
ORDER BY avg_score DESC;

spec.question: Which clause filters out groups AFTER `COUNT(*)` or `AVG(score)` has been computed?
spec.explanation: `HAVING` runs after `GROUP BY` so it can evaluate aggregate functions.

activities.title: Neovim Lab: Top AI Models by Average Eval Score

spec.instructions:
Tables:
- `models(id, name)`
- `runs(id, model_id, score)`

Write a SQL query in `query.sql` returning `(name, avg_score)` where `avg_score = ROUND(AVG(score), 2)` for models with `AVG(score) >= 0.80`, ordered by `avg_score DESC`.
hints: JOIN `runs r ON r.model_id = m.id`, then `GROUP BY m.name HAVING AVG(r.score) >= 0.80`.

modules.title: JSON Structure, Data Types & JSON Schema
modules.subtitle: Author strict, valid API payloads and structured LLM output schemas.
modules.summary: Avoid JSON pitfalls (trailing commas, single quotes) and craft payloads matching strict JSON Schema contracts.

sections.title: 1.1 Strict JSON Rules
sections.body: Unlike JavaScript objects, valid JSON strictly requires double-quoted keys and strings, forbids trailing commas, and forbids comments. JSON Schema lets APIs and AI structured-output pipelines validate every key and type automatically.

spec.question: Which snippet is 100% valid RFC 8259 JSON?
spec.explanation: RFC 8259 requires double-quoted keys and forbids trailing commas.

activities.title: Neovim Lab: Repair & Complete a Training Spec JSON

modules.title: Well-Formed XML, Attributes & XPath
modules.subtitle: Navigate hierarchical XML configs, SVGs, and structured prompts cleanly.
modules.summary: Build well-formed XML trees with attributes and verify them using real `lxml` XPath queries.

sections.title: 1.1 Elements, Attributes & XPath
sections.body: Every XML document must have exactly one root element, properly nested closing tags, and quoted attribute values. XPath (`//dataset[@split='eval']/name`) queries any depth declaratively.

spec.question: In XPath, what does `//task[@priority='high']` select?
options: Every `<task>` element anywhere in the document whose `priority` attribute equals `'high'`
spec.explanation: `//` searches recursively at any depth, and `[@attr='val']` filters by attribute value.
spec.hint: `@` always refers to an XML attribute.

modules.title: Regex: Anchors, Quantifiers & Named Capture Groups
modules.subtitle: Parse logs, refactor in Neovim, and extract structured fields in one line.
modules.summary: Build muscle memory for character classes (`\d`, `\w`), quantifiers (`+`, `{m,n}`), and Python/JS named groups `(?P<name>...)`.

sections.title: 1.1 Named Capture Groups
sections.body: Instead of brittle positional group indices (`match.group(2)`), use named capture groups `(?P<epoch>\d+)` in Python (or `(?<epoch>\d+)` in JS) to extract self-documenting dicts directly from messy logs.

spec.prompt: Match a 4-digit year followed by a hyphen and 2-digit month (`2026-11`).

activities.title: Neovim Lab: Extract Epoch & Loss from Training Logs

spec.instructions: Write a single-line regex in `pattern.regex` matching lines like `epoch=12 loss=0.341` with named groups `(?P<epoch>...)` and `(?P<loss>...)` (loss must contain a decimal point).

modules.title: Boss Project: URL Shortener & Click Analytics API
modules.subtitle: Multi-milestone FastAPI + SQLite project graded with real TestClient integration tests.
modules.summary: Build a real persistent URL shortener backed by SQLite, complete with click-counting redirects and analytics stats.

sections.title: Project Spec
sections.body: Complete each milestone in Neovim. Milestone 1 builds link creation & lookup; Milestone 2 adds click tracking and `/stats/{code}` analytics.

spec.instructions:
Build `shortener.py` with:
- `POST /shorten` accepting `{"url": "https://...", "code": "optional"}` -> returns `201` with `{"code": ..., "url": ..., "clicks": 0}`.
- `GET /links/{code}` -> increments `clicks` by 1 and returns `{"code": ..., "url": ..., "clicks": <new count>}` (or `404`).
- `GET /stats/{code}` -> returns current link stats WITHOUT incrementing `clicks` (or `404`).
spec.test_code:
from fastapi.testclient import TestClient
import shortener

def test_shortener_project():
    shortener.STORE.clear()
    c = TestClient(shortener.app)
    r = c.post('/shorten', json={'url': 'https://neovim.io', 'code': 'nvim'})
    assert r.status_code == 201
    assert r.json() == {'code': 'nvim', 'url': 'https://neovim.io', 'clicks': 0}

    r2 = c.get('/links/nvim')
    assert r2.status_code == 200 and r2.json()['clicks'] == 1
    r3 = c.get('/links/nvim')
    assert r3.status_code == 200 and r3.json()['clicks'] == 2

    st = c.get('/stats/nvim')
    assert st.status_code == 200 and st.json()['clicks'] == 2

    auto = c.post('/shorten', json={'url': 'https://fastapi.tiangolo.com'})
    assert auto.status_code == 201 and len(auto.json()['code']) >= 4
    assert c.get('/stats/nope').status_code == 404
hints: Generate an automatic code via `secrets.token_urlsafe(4)` when `payload.code` is None.

modules.title: Boss Project: AI Training Log Summary CLI

sections.title: Project Spec
sections.body: Given a training log containing lines like `epoch=1 loss=0.842`, print `best_epoch=<N> best_loss=<L>` for the lowest numeric loss.

activities.title: Milestone 1: Extract Best Epoch & Lowest Loss

spec.instructions:
Write `best_epoch.sh <logfile>` that parses lines formatted like `epoch=<int> loss=<float>` (ignoring other lines) and prints:
`best_epoch=<N> best_loss=<L>` for the minimum loss.

fixture_files.run.log:
INFO starting
epoch=1 loss=0.912
epoch=2 loss=0.415
WARN slow step
epoch=3 loss=0.490

hints: `awk` makes this a 5-line gem: match `/^epoch=/`, split `=` fields, track `min_loss` numerically (`loss + 0 < min_loss`).

modules.title: Boss Project: C++20 Fixed-Capacity Key-Value Ring/LRU
modules.subtitle: Build a fast C++20 LRU cache supporting O(1) lookup and eviction.
modules.summary: Combine `std::list` and `std::unordered_map` to implement a production-style LRU cache in C++20.

sections.title: Project Spec
sections.body: Implement `LRUCache` with `get(int key)` (returning `-1` if absent) and `put(int key, int val)` evicting the least-recently-used key when capacity is exceeded.

activities.title: Milestone 1: Implement O(1) LRUCache in C++20

spec.instructions: Implement `class LRUCache` in `lru.hpp` with constructor `LRUCache(size_t cap)`, `int get(int key)`, and `void put(int key, int value)`.
hints: Use `order_.splice(order_.begin(), order_, it->second)` to promote an entry to most-recently-used in O(1)!
